question: What security findings and enforcement policy should OpenClaw adopt for prompt-bearing Markdown across workspace bootstrap ingestion, SKILL.md loading, and ClawHub install or publishing paths?
rationale: Pattern selection, acceptable false-positive rates, runtime blocking, user overrides, upgrade compatibility, and the ownership split between core and ClawHub are security and product-policy choices that source inspection cannot resolve safely.

options.title: Shared findings, staged enforcement
options.body: Define a shared structured finding taxonomy, initially warn or tag at runtime and ClawHub boundaries, and enable blocking only for narrowly proven high-confidence findings after compatibility proof.

options.title: Mandatory fail-closed validation
options.body: Reject prompt-bearing Markdown with prohibited findings during runtime ingestion and installation, accepting that existing skills and workspaces may require remediation or explicit overrides.

options.title: ClawHub-only policy
options.body: Enforce scanning and labeling only during ClawHub publishing or installation while leaving local workspace prompt ingestion unchanged.

recommendation.title: Shared findings, staged enforcement
recommendation.body: Define a shared structured finding taxonomy, initially warn or tag at runtime and ClawHub boundaries, and enable blocking only for narrowly proven high-confidence findings after compatibility proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has recent history across the central code paths and already participated in defining the remaining cross-boundary decision on the issue.
